body:
Good morning, Kern County. It’s Monday, September 14, and we’re starting the week with a bit of history worth celebrating: two Arvin High School staff members have been named winners of the prestigious Yale Educator Award. Skies are clear and calm this morning after a busy night for local emergency crews, with temperatures sitting at a mild 63 degrees at Meadows Field and no active alerts on the horizon for the valley.

## The Kern Overnight

The night in Kern County was busy for first responders, with the most significant call coming just before dawn. Fire crews were dispatched shortly after 5 a.m. to a vegetation fire burning near the Union Pacific Railroad tracks north of Highway 58. The assignment grew quickly as two engines, three patrol units, a water tender, and two dozers were called in, along with multiple battalion chiefs, a division supervisor, and a safety officer. A helicopter was placed on standby, and air-to-ground coordination was requested if needed, with additional strike-team resources held ready as the fire burned in the rail corridor.

Earlier in the night, a pursuit through town kept officers occupied. Around 12:09 a.m., a chase ran westbound along California Avenue, with speeds called out from roughly 60 to 95 mph. Dispatchers noted light traffic and no pedestrians as the vehicle turned off the avenue, headed north, and eventually pulled into a residence parking lot where units moved in. Just after 2 a.m., a separate pursuit ended at a home and prompted a neighborhood search. Officers checked a backyard and an attic after one person was reported in the backyard and a second was last seen walking west. A K-9 unit and additional officers fanned out on foot, checking spots where someone might hide.

In the river bottom, crews spent part of the evening on a brush fire burning in heavy grass and brush. Reported around 10:37 p.m., the fire covered roughly a quarter to a half-acre and moved slowly while crews weighed how to reach it. Access from the river side was being considered as additional resources were requested. And around 4:06 a.m., a tractor-trailer went down in the number four lane of southbound Interstate 5, with the driver out placing warning triangles and a second semi on the right shoulder. Units at the scene asked for a heavy-duty tow to clear the crash.

The overnight log also included a domestic disturbance at Roseman Mobile Home Park just after midnight, in which the caller reported a man with access to a firearm refusing to let her leave; a report from a juvenile on a Quincy Street block who alleged her mother battered her; a shots-heard call in central Bakersfield tied to a prior weapons report; and an open-line call from a Delwood Avenue block that disconnected with no answer on callback.

## Today's weather

Expect a pleasant late-summer day across Kern County. The high today should reach near 86 degrees, with overnight lows settling around 63. It's currently 63 degrees at Meadows Field (KBFL), with no active weather alerts for the area. Air quality is measured at 51, which lands in the moderate range — fine for most outdoor plans, though sensitive groups may want to take it easy during the peak of the afternoon. The weekend's cooling trend, fueled by a North Pacific trough easing SoCal heat, is expected to carry into the week ahead, keeping things comfortable.

## Top stories

**Two staff members from Arvin High School have made history as recipients of the 2026 Yale Educator Award, a first for the school.** According to 23ABC, math teacher Matthew Regpala and counselor Gerardo Guzman were both nominated by Yaquelin Acosta, a freshman at Yale University majoring in theater. Regpala said he had no idea he was nominated and found out just days ago, with his family excited knowing how much he invests in his students. Guzman said the recognition caught him off guard but means a great deal, as his goal as a counselor is to help students reach their full potential regardless of their circumstances. Both credited Acosta's growth during her years at Arvin High as a rewarding part of the recognition.

**Over 1,500 participants took part in the Kern County Cancer Foundation's annual Kern Cancer Run/Walk on Saturday at the Park at Riverwalk.** KERO 23ABC reports that more than 200 cancer survivors were among those in attendance. Melody Saberon Ibarra, a survivor helping at an event booth, shared that she was first diagnosed in 1996 with liver sarcoma, then again three years later with epithelioid sarcoma, and has now been cancer-free for over two decades. She credited the foundation with being a blessing during her treatment, noting she was a young college student with no income at the time. Executive director Michelle Avila said the annual event alone has raised over $2 million, and the foundation pays patient bills — sometimes as much as $10,000 — so patients can focus on treatment and recovery. Trella Linley, another survivor, said the foundation that once helped her is now helping her son, who is currently going through cancer treatments.

**KGET 17 reports that an Air Force colonel is sharing what he calls a "modern-day miracle" story of survival after his jet was shot down over Iran.** The detailed account, featured by the outlet, covers how the colonel managed to survive the incident and make it back. It's a remarkable narrative of resilience that underscores the risks faced by military aviators in hostile territory.

**Americans are shopping secondhand again, and KGET 17 takes a look at what's behind the boom.** The report explores the growing popularity of thrift and resale shopping, examining the economic and environmental factors driving consumers back to secondhand stores. For valley families watching budgets, the trend offers more affordable options for clothing and goods while also keeping items out of landfills — a shift that appears to have staying power this time around.

## Something good

**A study highlighted by KGET 17 found that a compound in blueberries may help muscles burn fat more efficiently.** While the research is preliminary, it's a pleasant reminder that the season's fruit brings more than just flavor — those farmers-market blueberries might be doing your body a favor beyond the taste.

**The Arvin High School Yale Educator Award win is the kind of news that makes a community proud.** Two educators, nominated by a former student now thriving at an Ivy League university, is a testament to the impact of dedicated teachers and counselors in the south valley. It's a well-deserved moment in the spotlight for Regpala and Guzman, and for the school that helped shape a Yale freshman along the way.

## Coming up this week

It's a busy week for public meetings across Bakersfield. The Fire Civil Service Commission meets this afternoon at 3 p.m., and the City Council holds two sessions Wednesday — a closed session at 3:30 p.m. followed by the regular open meeting at 5:15 p.m. On Tuesday, the Development Streamlining Ad Hoc Committee convenes at noon, with the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission meeting at 2 p.m. and the Historic Preservation Commission at 4 p.m. The Planning Commission meets Thursday at 5:30 p.m., and the Finance, Economic Development and Jobs Committee wraps up the week Monday, Sept. 21, at noon.

For entertainment, the historic Fox Theater has plenty on the calendar. Tonight brings "Cults & Classics: FARGO" — a fittingly dark comedy for a Monday night. Friday night hosts "It's A 2000s Party," and next Monday offers "Cults & Classics: What Ever Happened to Baby Jane?" The theater also has MEN I TRUST with special guest Evan Wright coming up Sept. 23 and MIKE SHERM on Sept. 26. Season passes for the Cults & Classics 2026-2027 series are available now for regulars who want to lock in their seats for the year ahead.
